scenes.headline: How a drifting mean logit becomes a loss spike
scenes.sub: Chen, Goldblum and colleagues on time-bomb spikes in the LM head
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Mantissa! Some training runs look healthy for most of their budget, then climb and never recover. Here is why.

scenes.text: Adam slowly shifts every logit by the same amount. That is harmless in exact maths, but BF16 cannot keep small differences between huge numbers.
scenes.say: Adam shifts every logit by the same amount. Exact maths does not care. BF16 does.

steps.say: Rare tokens get small gradients that push them down, step after step.
Adam scales those up to full steps, so the mean logit slides.
The head writes its logits in BF16, where the gap between numbers grows with their size.
Near a thousand, neighbours are eight apart. The differences the softmax needs are rounded away, and the loss climbs.

scenes.title: The gradient that sums to zero
scenes.text: sum over vocab of (p - y) h = 0
scenes.say: Why does Adam push? Sum the head's gradient over the vocabulary.

parts.say: Probabilities and the target each sum to one, so this sums to zero.

parts.note: momentum keeps it, Adam's division breaks it
parts.say: Momentum S G D keeps the zero. Adam divides each row by its own scale, and the rows stop cancelling.

scenes.title: The fix lives in the head's optimizer

left.title: AdamW everywhere
left.say: With AdamW on the head, the mean drifts and the error grows.

right.title: SGD-M on the head
items: Same linear map for every row
right.say: Train only the head with momentum S G D, and the mean stays put.

steps.say: In the paper, BF16 true fails first, BF16 mixed later, and FP32 survives.
The rounding error climbs before each failure. With momentum S G D, it stays flat.

scenes.title: Final loss in my CPU toy
scenes.note: LM head only, simulated BF16, one seed, 40,000 steps
scenes.say: In my CPU toy, the same drift was harmless in FP32 and costly in BF16. Removing the mean fixed it.

scenes.text: Watch the mean logit and the BF16 error. Keep the mean near zero and BF16 is enough.
scenes.say: Log the mean logit and the BF16 error. Keep the mean near zero.

recap: Adam breaks the head's zero-sum gradient
Large logits lose their differences in BF16
Momentum SGD on the head keeps the mean
scenes.say: Adam drifts the mean, BF16 rounds away the differences, and momentum on the head holds the mean still.
